The +36.5% reported Q1 FY2026 operating income print is entirely a one-time item. The 10-Q (filed 2026-06-11, period ended May 2, 2026) explicitly discloses a $19.1M interchange fee litigation settlement booked as a credit to selling expenses — a 660 bps benefit to op margin. Stripping it: adjusted op income is $40.4M vs $43.5M prior year, or -7.3% YoY. Adjusted op margin falls to 14.0% from 16.0%. Ex-settlement, SG&A rose 150 bps (incentive comp + store labor inflating faster than revenue). Gross margin compressed 50 bps on merchandise pressure. Annual trend confirms no inflection: op margin peaked at 24.4% in FY2023, has declined to ~20% and the cost structure remains the headwind. Revenue comps are genuinely positive (+5.1% with AUR +4.3%) but insufficient to offset the cost bleed. Not a blowup (zero debt, $251M operating cash flow, near-52-week-low price), but the EBIT-growth thesis predicate is false — this is a value trap on settlement-inflated TTM earnings with structurally compressing underlying profitability.

EBIT growth is ~98% commodity price variance ($36.8M of $37.5M revenue gain from price), zero operational improvement. Q1 2026 ammonia gate +24% and UAN gate +34% YoY driven by Iran conflict supply disruption (Strait of Hormuz ~30% global N transit) plus pre-existing 2H 2025 tightening — geopolitical and cyclical, not structural. Historical EBIT cycle confirms: 2022 peak $320M → 2024 trough $90M (72% collapse) on same asset base; Q4 2025 posted -$2.9M EBIT just one quarter prior, proving how quickly earnings disappear off-season. Three near-term destroyers: (1) East Dubuque turnaround August 2026 = $30-35M direct cost plus lost production, likely negative Q3 EBIT; (2) no hedge book — pure commodity exposure; (3) $4/quarter distribution is a commodity yield trap (cut 82% 2022→2024). Stock already re-rated to all-time high $134 in March on the Iran spike, now at $111 — upside already captured. Not ownable without a durable view on nitrogen prices above $350/ton UAN through 2027.
